items.name: Yvar 100mm f/3.3 (YVENT)
items.description: Telephoto lens with 4x magnification compared to a standard 25mm focal length lens; visifocus depth of field scale. Introduced in 1950. from.heading: D Mount Lenses for 8mm Cameras

items.name: Yvar 150mm f/4 (YVONG)
items.description: Extreme telephoto lens, approximately 7 1/2 inches in length with a weight of 7.5 ounces. It was introduced in 1950 and came complete with a leather carrying case and shoulder strap. A detachable lens shade was also included. Because of its over-all length, it was recommended only as an accessory lens and not intended to be mounted with lenses of shorter focal lengths.

items.description: A moderately wide angle lens with Visifocus scale; normal C Mount.

items.description: Standard focal length lens; Visifocus scale.

from.heading: C and RX Mount Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Pan Cinor 20mm-60mm f/2.8 Zoom Lens with Viewfinder (PANCI)
items.description: A C mount zoom lens with an attached viewfinder, introduced in 1953. The field shown in the parallax corrected viewfinder was coupled to the focal length distance of the lens.

from.heading: C and RX Mount Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Pan Cinor 12.5mm-36mm f/2.8 zoom lens (HUPAN)
items.description: A D mount zoom lens with an attached viewfinder. Introduced in 1954; sometimes referred to as the "Pan Cinor 36".

from.heading: D Mount Lenses for 8mm Cameras

items.name: Switar 16mm f/1.8 (st. SWESE, RX DAESE)
items.description: This Visifocus lens was introduced in 1954, with a standard C mount (SWESE); a RX mount version (DAESE) was available in 1956.

from.heading: C and RX Mount Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Switar 5.5mm f/1.8 (SWINQ)
items.description: Wide angle lens, introduced in 1954.

from.heading: D Mount Lenses for 8mm Cameras

items.name: Switar 50mm f/1.4 (St. SWIFI, RX DAIFI)
items.description: A telephoto lens that was available in both standard c-mount and "RX" mount; the standard version (SWIFI) was introduced in 1954, while the RX mount version (DAIFI) was introduced in 1956. It came with a detachable lens shade.

from.heading: C and RX Mount Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Yvar Filtin 12.5mm f/2.8 (FILTI)
items.description: This lens was introduced in 1954 and contained four (4) built in filters; yellow, red, "daylight" and "skylight". Filters could be selected by turning a knurled index ring. Four "no filter" positions were marked between each filter position. The Filtin could focus from 1 1/2 feet to infinity and close down to f/22.

from.heading: D Mount Lenses for 8mm Cameras

items.name: Pan Cinor 70 (17.5mm-70mm f/2.4) Zoom Lens with viewfinder)
items.description: Introduced in 1955, this lens offered a built-in viewfinder which offered through-the-lens viewing and framing of the subject. Pan Cinor 100 (25mm-100mm f/3.4) The Pan Cinor 100 was available in the same year, and offered an increased focal length of 25mm-100m, but at a slightly lower speed of f/3.4. It is otherwise similar in appearance to the Pan Cinor 70 (pictured above).

from.heading: C and RX Mount Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Switar 10mm f/1.6 (st. SWEDI, RX DAADI)
items.description: These wide angle lenses were introduced in 1956. Two versions were available; in standard C mount for non-reflex cameras (SWEDI) and in RX mount for the H-16 Reflex (DAADI).

from.heading: C and RX Mount Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Pizar 25mm f/1.5 RX
items.description: Standard focal length lens with Visifocus DOF scale, introduced in 1957; in "RX mount" for H-16 reflex cameras.

from.heading: C and RX Mount Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Pizar 5.5mm f/2 (also f/1.9) (PIZUI)
items.description: Wide angle lens with fixed focus and a maximum aperture of f/2; introduced in 1957. A later version was available in 1959; it had a maximum aperture of f/1.9. Both were fixed focus lenses and were identical in appearance.

from.heading: D Mount Lenses for 8mm Cameras

items.name: Pan Cinor 30 DV (10mm-30mm f/2.8)
items.description: Introduced in 1958, the Pan Cinor 30 "Direct View" zoom lens had a built-in zoom lever and adjustable viewfinder. It was available in standard D mount with a zoom range of 10mm-30mm focal length.

from.heading: D Mount Lenses for 8mm Cameras

items.name: Pan Cinor 85 (17mm-85mm f/2) C mount
items.description: The Pan Cinor 85 was introduced in 1959. It was designed for use with H-16 cameras. The attached viewfinder featured a split-image rangefinder focusing aid. Although it's similar in appearance to the earlier Pan Cinor series, it is identifiable by a black finish.

from.heading: C and RX Mount Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Pizar 50mm f/1.8 Visifocus (St. and RX versions)
items.yearNote: 'Introduced in the late 1959.' Missed by the patterns because of the stray 'the'.
items.description: Introduced in the late 1959, this telephoto lens was available in both C mount and RX mount; both with a Visifocus DOF scale.

from.heading: C and RX Mount Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Switar 13mm f/0.9 Visifocus
items.description: A very fast lens of standard focal length, introduced in 1959.

from.heading: D Mount Lenses for 8mm Cameras

items.name: Switar 36mm f/1.8 Visifocus
items.description: A fast telephoto lens, introduced in 1959. It came with a detachable lens hood.

from.heading: D Mount Lenses for 8mm Cameras

items.name: Yvar 13mm f/1.8 Visifocus
items.description: This standard focal length lens, introduced in 1959, used the Visifocus depth of field scale.

from.heading: D Mount Lenses for 8mm Cameras

items.name: Angenieux 120 (f/2.2 12-120)
items.description: C mount versions of the Angenieux 120 were available that were optically corrected for Bolex reflex cameras; these were marked RX near the base. A built in geared crank allowed slow zooms, while a detachable 1" rod permitted faster zooms. The 120 used a standard Seriex IX filter and was approximately 1 pound, 12 ounces.

from.heading: C Mount Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Angenieux 120 BDA (f/2.2 12-120 auto diaphragm)
items.description: Optically corrected versions of this lens were recommended for H-16 reflex cameras. The lens featured an automatic diaphragm with built in exposure meter; it was powered by either two (2) TR132 or four (4) RM-1 batteries. The TR132 was a 2.7V battery, while the RM-1 was a 1.35V battery; both were mercury cell, and both have been discontinued. However, the auto diaphragm could be switched off and adjusted manually from f/2.2 to f/22. It could be fitted with Series IX filters and weighed 2 lbs and 12 oz.

from.heading: C Mount Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Angenieux 120 w/ Viewfinder (f/2.2 12-120)
items.description: This version of the Angenieux 120 was equipped with a viewfinder and designed for C mount cameras; Bolex recommended its use with the H-16 M and H-16 S non-reflex series. It used a Series IX filter and weighed 2 lbs, 6 oz.

from.heading: C Mount Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Angenieux 95 w/ Viewfinder / f/2.2 9.5-95mm
items.description: This version of the Angenieux 95 was designed for C-mount cameras and recommended for use with the H-16M series. The viewfinder had a ground glass focusing aid and was designed to fit over the top of H model cameras. Shown here, it is attached to an H-16 S-4, with a built in turret support. Weight was approximately 3 1/2 lbs. Filter size: 103.5mm Angenieux 95 f/2.2 9.5-95mm This version was optically corrected for Bolex H-16 reflex cameras. It was otherwise the same lens, but without the viewfinder. A built in geared crank allowed slow zooms; a 1" lever could be attached for faster zooms. Weight was approximately 2 lbs, 12 oz. Filter size: 103.5mm

from.heading: C Mount Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Macro Switar 12.5 f/1.3 H8 rx
items.description: Standard focal length lens for the H-8 REX; pre-set diaphragm with Visifocus DOF scale and built in macro extension. Focus from 3" to infinity. Uses Series V filters; detachable lens hood.

from.heading: Lenses for H-8 Reflex Cameras

items.name: Macro Switar 36mm f/1.4 H8 rx
items.description: Telephoto lens for the H-8 REX; pre-set diaphragm with Visifocus DOF scale and built in macro extension. Focus from 10 1/2" to infinity. Uses Series V filters; detachable lens hood.

from.heading: Lenses for H-8 Reflex Cameras

items.name: Macro Yvar 150mm f/3.3
items.description: The Macro Yvar 150mm was redesigned in 1970 to include a pre-set diaphragm. It also featured Visifocus DOF scale and built in macro extension. Minimum focus distance: 6 feet. Minimum diaphragm setting: f/32. Accepts Series VI drop in filters.

from.heading: C and RX Mount Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Pan Cinor 40 / Pan Cinor 40 R
items.description: This lens was available in two versions; both were introduced in 1960 and offered through the lens viewing with an adjustable finder, a zoom range of 8mm to 40mm and a speed of f/1.9. The 40R version featured a split image rangefinder focusing aid, and was slightly more expensive.

from.heading: Lenses for 8mm Cameras

items.name: Switar 5.5mm f/1.6 H8 rx
items.description: Wide angle lens, specifically designed for the H-8 REX camera. It featured a pre-set diaphragm, Visifocus depth of field scale and minimum focusing distance of 4 1/2 inches. Series V filters could be attached.

from.heading: Lenses for H-8 Reflex Cameras

items.name: Vario Switar 86
items.description: Introduced in 1961; designed specifically for H-16 reflex cameras. It incorporated an automatic pre-set diaphragm feature which opened the diaphragm for viewing and focusing and closed it automatically prior to exposure. The pre-set aperture control and camera release mechanism were combined with a zoom lever; this could be couple to the Declic H grip with a special accessory cable (not shown). Zoom range from 18-86mm; maximum aperture f/2.5, minimum aperture f/22. The lens could accept Series VIII filters and weighed 2 lbs and 4 oz.

from.heading: C and RX Mount Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Macro Yvar 150mm f/3.3
items.description: Introduced in 1962; C mount, extreme telephoto lens with Visifocus DOF scale and built in macro extension. Minimum focus distance of 6 feet; minimum aperture of f/32. Accepts Series VI drop in filters.
items.listingNote: The archive carries two entries for the Macro Yvar 150mm f/3.3, this one and a later redesign. The code and price are attached here, to the 1962 original, because the 1965 list predates the redesign.

from.heading: C and RX Mount Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Pan Cinor 40 RX
items.description: Introduced in 1962 and designed for the H-8 REX. It offered a 5:1 zoom range from 8mm to 40mm, with a maximum aperture of f/1.9.

from.heading: Lenses for 8mm Cameras

items.name: Vario Switar 36 f/1.9 (8mm-36mm)
items.description: Introduced in 1962 and designed by Kern for the H-8 reflex. It incorporated an automatic pre-set diaphragm feature which opened the diaphragm for viewing and focusing and closed it automatically prior to exposure. The pre-set aperture control and camera release mechanism were combined with a zoom lever; this could be couple to the Declic H grip with a special accessory cable (not shown). It could accept Series VI filters and weighed 13.5 ounces.

from.heading: Lenses for H-8 Reflex Cameras

items.name: Macro Yvar 100mm f/2.8
items.description: Introduced in 1963; C mount telephoto lens with Visifocus depth of field scale and built in macro extension. Minimum focus distance of 4 feet. Accepts Series VI drop in filters.

from.heading: C and RX Mount Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Macro Switar 50mm f/1.4 Rx
items.description: Telephoto lens for H-16 reflex cameras, introduced in 1964. Pre set diaphragm, Visifocus DOF scale, built in macro extension and minimum focus distance of 15".

from.heading: C and RX Mount Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Pan Cinor 85 Compact (f/3.8 17mm-85mm)
items.description: This zoom lens was introduced in 1964 and designed specifically for H-16 reflex cameras. The compact size permitted permitted its use in conjuction with other lenses on the turret. It featured a built in zoom lever with 5:1 zoom range from 17mm to 85mm and a minimum aperture of f/22. The lens could focus from 3 1/2 feet to infinity and weighed approximately 10 ounces. It could accept Series VII filters.

from.heading: Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Pan Cinor 85-2 (f/2 17mm-85mm)
items.description: Introduced in 1964, the Pan Cinor 85-2 zoom lens had a built in reflex viewfinder with a coincident image rangefinder focusing aid. The viewfinder had an adjustable eyepiece and was supplied with a rubber eyecup; it could be placed over the top of non reflex H-16 cameras, or placed at a 45° angle on H-16 reflex cameras. The lens came with a detachable shade and zoom lever and could accept Series VIII filters. Minimum focus distance: 6 feet. Minimum aperture: f/16. Weight: 2 lbs. 4 oz. This lens was also available in C mount for Auricon cine cameras; this version had an extended viewfinder of approximately 10 inches (2" longer than the H-16 version).

from.heading: Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Vario Switar 36EE (8mm-36mm f/1.9)
items.description: The Vario Switar 36EE ("Electric Eye") was introduced in 1964. It featured a fully automatic diaphragm control with a cadmium sulphide photo resistor which was sensitive to film ratings from 10-400 ASA. The exposure meter was powered by one (1) PX-13 1.35v mercury cell battery. The lens could be fitted with Series VI filters and weighed 18 ounces.

from.heading: Lenses for H-8 Reflex Cameras

items.name: Vario Switar 86EE (18mm-86mm f/2.5)
items.description: This lens was introduced in 1964, as the first "Electric Eye" 16mm zoom lens. It was designed specifically for H-16 reflex cameras and featured a fully automatic diaphragm control with a cadmium sulphide photo resistor which was sensitive to film ratings from 10-400 ASA. The exposure meter was powered by one (1) PX-13 1.35v mercury cell battery. Minimum aperture of f/16. Weight: 2 lbs, 4 oz. Accepts Series VIII filters.

from.heading: C and RX Mount Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Macro Switar 26mm f/1.1 RX
items.description: Standard focal length lens with built in macro extension, pre set diaphragm, Visifocus DOF scale and minimum focus distance of 7 1/2". Introduced in 1968 for use with H-16 reflex cameras.

from.heading: C and RX Mount Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Switar 10mm f/1.6 RX
items.description: Wide angle lens with pre-set diaphragm, vVisifocus depth of field scale and minimum focus distance of 1". Introduced in 1968 for use with H-16 reflex cameras.

from.heading: C and RX Mount Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Vario-Switar 86-OE (18mm-86mm f/2.5)
items.description: The 86-OE was introduced in 1968. It featured an automatic diaphragm, but unlike the 86EE, exposure measurements were taken through the lens. The built in meter was sensitive to film speeds from 10 to 200 ASA and powered by one (1) PX-13 1.35v mercury cell battery. Minimum aperture: f/16. Weight: approximately 2 1/2 lbs. Accepts Series VIII filters.

from.heading: C and RX Mount Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Macro-Switar 75mm f/1.9
items.description: C mount Telephoto lens, introduced in 1970. Pre set diaphragm, Visifocus DOF scale, built in macro extension and minimum focus distance of 5 feet.

from.heading: C and RX Mount Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Pan Cinor 120 (f/3.3 12-120 no viewfinder)
items.description: The Pan Cinor 120 was introduced in 1970 for H-16 reflex cameras. It had a maximum aperture of f/3.3 and could be stopped down to f/32 or fully closed. The diaphragm, zoom and focus rings could all be control with separate levers. The lens had a 10:1 zoom range of 12mm to 120mm with a minimum focus distance of 4 1/4 feet (approximately 1.3 meters). The detachable lens shade could hold Series VIII filters. Lens weight: 1 lb. 11 oz.

from.heading: Lenses for H-16 Cameras

items.name: Vario Switar 100 POE (f/1.9 16-100mm)
items.description: Introduced in 1970, the Kern Vario Switar 100 POE featured through the lens exposure and power zoom control. The exposure meter was powered by one (1) PX1 1.35v mercury cell battery; power for the zoom motor was supplied by two (2) RM1 1.35V mercury batteries batteries. It accepts series IX filters and weighs approximately 3 lbs.

from.heading: C and RX Mount Lenses for H-16 Cameras
